newsitem.title: BRAZIL: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN CAN SETTLE 500CC WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN CAN SETTLE 500CC WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Australia's Michael Doohan has a chance to conclude this year's 500cc world championship on Sunday.
The Brazilian Grand Prix offers Doohan the chance to win his seventh consecutive race -- ninth of the season -- and his fourth consecutive world title.
Doohan is so far ahead of the field that he could settle the title with five races remaining if he finishes first and second-placed Nobuatsu Aoki of Japan is third or worse.
Second place could even be enough, depending on how his nearest rivals perform.
The Australian's win at the Nuerburgring in Germany on July 20 took him to 220 points, a massive lead of 107 over Honda team mate Aoki.
Japan's Tadayuki Okada, another Honda rider, is a further four points behind in third place. But the chances of the two Japanese riders are nothing more than mathematical.
Doohan has outclassed the opposition all season and now seems certain to equal Mike Hailwood and Giacomo Agostini's records of four successive crowns.
He had already won the championship by the time the circus came to Brazil last year, but the Rio race has been brought forward in the calender.

Local support for the event, at a circuit which is in an awkward location on the outskirts of Rio, has never been great and this year organisers have slashed the entrance prices from $60 to just under five in a bid to bring in fans.
But ticket sales were still reported to be slow this week.
